column1: # aionas-savings: the noisy-command guard rules and the long-output store
# settings (AIO-860). Versioned: bump "version" on every change.
# Fields are separated by ONE tab. Lines starting with "#" are comments.
#   setting <TAB> name <TAB> value
#   rule <TAB> id <TAB> kind <TAB> match <TAB> skip <TAB> insert
# A rule applies only to a simple command: one program, no | ; & < > ` $(
# and no newline. Leading NAME=value words are kept in front of it.
#   match   POSIX ERE on the command after those words. It must match at the
#           start and end at a word boundary; the flags are inserted there.
#   skip    POSIX ERE tried on the rest of the command plus one space; when
#           it matches, the command is already quiet and nothing changes.
#           "-" means never.
#   insert  the flags of the quiet form, or "-" for none.
#   kind    quiet: the command is rewritten to the quiet form. A failing run
#                  shows everything the quiet form prints.
#           cap:   the command is not changed. A run that succeeds with more
#                  than cap_tokens of output is cut to whole lines within
#                  cap_tokens, ending with "[aionas-guard: capped <id> ..."
#                  (the post-tool hook does it); a failing run keeps its
#                  full output.
# Every rewrite starts with "AIONAS_GUARD=<id> ". AIONAS_FULL=1 in front of
# a command skips the guard and the store (counted as a bypass).
# No backslashes in match or skip: awk reads them as dynamic regexps.
